data.description: Company-wide comms layer so the investor can talk to agents directly and employees can communicate. Decided by investor interview 2026-08-29: (1) Interface: LOCAL WEB APP — localhost server + browser UI; no external hosting, respects no-DigitalOcean/no-purchase constraints. (2) Delivery model: INBOX AT SESSION START — messages persist in a store; agents read their inbox/channels when a session spins up; orchestrators relay mid-session; no daemons in v1 (live wake-up may be a future project). (3) Process: FULL COMPANY PROCESS — cto-owen owns as CTO, cofounders scope (ceo-carla product spec, cto-owen technical plan), first employee hires (e.g. developer, QA personas) per CLAUDE.md hiring convention; hires recorded in personnel/ (HR is out of Lattice scope, but this dev project is in). (4) v1 scope, all must-have: named channels, DMs (human-agent and agent-agent), threaded replies, Lattice integration (messages reference tasks; task events can post to a channel). The user-visible app must let the investor participate directly per CLAUDE.md. Store must be readable/writable by both the web UI and agent CLI/file access. Tech stack: CTO's call.
data.title: Internal chat app (Slack-type) v1 — channels, DMs, threads, Lattice integration

data.description: Two non-blocking findings from the AS-2 QA review (qa-priya): (1) store.markRead accepts an upTo watermark beyond the current max message id — should clamp or reject; (2) CLI 'chat history @identity' and 'chat read @identity' get-or-create the DM conversation row on what should be a pure read. Neither violates any AS-2 acceptance criterion; both are small correctness/hygiene fixes in apps/chat/lib/store.js and apps/chat/bin/chat.js.
data.title: Chat app: tighten markRead bounds + make CLI reads side-effect-free

data.description: Investor directive 2026-08-29 (recorded in CLAUDE.md ## Infra): all local apps run via Docker / Docker Compose — no code runs bare on the host. Apply to apps/chat (the only app so far): compose file to build/run the server (loopback-only exposure preserved), persistent volume or bind mount for the SQLite data dir, read access to .lattice/ for event ingestion, and a containerized path for BOTH the test suite and the agent-facing chat CLI (agents must invoke it without running node on the host — e.g. docker compose run/exec wrapper). Update apps/chat README run instructions accordingly. Constraints: official images only, no registries requiring accounts/spend, no egress beyond image pulls, do not touch existing GitHub repos or DO services. Forward-looking: this compose setup should be the template for eventual DO hosting per CLAUDE.md Infra.
data.title: Containerize chat app: docker compose is the only way code runs

data.description: Chat messages live only in apps/chat/data/chat.db (gitignored, WAL mode, single machine, no backup). Decision (Forrest + investor chat, 2026-08-30): make chat history durable by committing append-only JSONL exports to the repo. Design already decided: (1) add a 'chat export' subcommand to apps/chat/bin/chat.js that dumps per-conversation append-only JSONL to a tracked directory (e.g. apps/chat/data/export/ — un-ignore that path), deterministic ordering so re-runs diff cleanly; (2) wire an export+commit step into the /advance tick procedure (.claude/commands/advance.md) at the point where master is pushed after a merged task — NOT a git pre-push hook (hooks that mutate create commits that miss the in-flight push) and NOT PR-open (our flow has no PRs, local --no-ff merges only); (3) add the export path to .gitattributes merge=union alongside Lattice events; (4) add a carve-out to CLAUDE.md Git Methodology for operational record commits (suggested format: 'records: chat export <date>') since these recurring commits belong to no single task. Acceptance: chat export is idempotent, export files round-trip the messages table faithfully (authors, threads, timestamps), /advance documents the step, methodology updated.
data.title: Chat history durability: JSONL export committed to git

data.description: Investor request via DM (human:forrest, 2026-08-30, @human:forrest msg 39): 'There should be a founder/investor/c level/board channel so I can talk to you and carla. also, dm selection should be a typeahead list'. Two chat-app features: (1) a #board channel restricted to human:forrest, agent:ceo-carla, agent:cto-owen — note the current schema has no channel membership concept (channels are all-visible; only DMs have members), so this needs a small membership mechanism or a private-channel type, not just a seeded channel name; (2) the web UI's DM identity selector becomes a typeahead over registered identities. CTO judgment: low complexity, real value, but does not preempt AS-5. Owner: whoever plans it should confirm restricted-visibility semantics (hidden vs read-only for non-members) with Forrest if ambiguous.
data.title: Chat: #board channel (restricted membership) + DM typeahead

data.description: Decision (Forrest, 2026-08-30, recorded in CLAUDE.md Operating Modes): sending a message in the chat app should trigger one /advance tick when no agent loop is already running. Goal: the chat app becomes Forrest's primary interface with the company; Claude Code chat recedes to governance/meta. Design constraints discovered so far: (1) The chat app runs only via docker compose (AS-4); a container cannot spawn a claude session on the host, so the trigger needs a HOST-SIDE watcher (launchd agent or supervised script) — keep it tiny. (2) Signal channel: compose bind-mounts ./data, so the server/store can touch a sentinel file (e.g. data/last-human-message) on insert of a message authored by human:* — the host watcher (fswatch or cheap polling) reacts to that; do NOT trigger on agent-authored messages. (3) Single-flight lock shared with the loop: if a /loop or a tick is already active, the watcher no-ops — the running tick's inbox pull delivers the message (suggested: a lockfile the watcher, /advance, and /loop-mode ticks all respect; document it in advance.md). (4) Debounce bursts (10-30s) so a rapid multi-message send fires one tick, not N. (5) Fire via headless invocation: claude -p '/advance' from the repo root; investigate permission-mode requirements for unattended runs and document what the host must have configured. Acceptance: with nothing running, a DM sent from the browser UI produces exactly one tick that reads the inbox and acts; with a loop running, no extra tick fires; agent-authored messages never trigger; watcher survives reboot (launchd) or documents how to start it.
data.title: Message-triggered /advance: chat app becomes the investor's primary interface

data.description:
Board request via DM (human:forrest, @human:forrest msg 50, 2026-08-30), verbatim: 'I think another useful thing would be that the direct messages shows ALL employees with their current work status. lets ship these internal improvements first so we can streamline work later'. Same message, also on the record: 'unlike most businesses, we have unlimited resources for internal tools.'

CTO framing (what/why — the plan is the planner's job): today the web UI's DM section lists only conversations that already exist; there is no company roster. Replace/augment it with a roster of ALL employees, each with current work status. Both data sources already live on disk: (1) roster = personnel/ dossier YAML frontmatter (actor_id, name, title, class, team, status) — the org-chart source of truth per CLAUDE.md; filter to status: active; (2) work status = derived from Lattice, which the chat server already reads read-only at /repo/.lattice (apps/chat/lib/lattice.js) — e.g. tasks assigned to the actor with their statuses ('AS-5: planned'), or 'idle' when nothing is in flight. Constraint the planner must resolve: compose mounts only ./data and .lattice into the container — personnel/ is not mounted, so roster access needs a mount (read-only, like .lattice) or another mechanism. Clicking a roster entry should get-or-create the DM. Overlaps AS-6's DM typeahead — coordinate; a full roster may subsume the typeahead for employee identities (typeahead still matters if identities outgrow one list). Optional cheap parity: a 'chat roster' CLI subcommand. Keep the zero-dependency rule: Node 24 stdlib only, Docker-only execution (AS-4).
data.title: Chat: DM sidebar shows all employees with current work status

data.description:
Board request via DM (chat msg 59, human:forrest): "I think we need query string to keep page context in here. also, the lattice events should link to the lattice site" — this task is the first half (query-string page context); the dashboard-link half is tracked separately.

Problem: apps/chat/public/app.js keeps all selection state (current channel/DM, open thread) in memory only. A refresh drops the user back to 'Select a conversation', and there is no way to share a link that opens a specific channel, DM, or thread.

Scope: encode page context in the URL query string (e.g. ?conv=...&thread=...) — update it on selection (history.replaceState/pushState, no full navigations), restore it on load after identities/conversations arrive, and reconcile with the existing location.hash msg-anchor behavior in openThread/closeThread (fold it in or keep it compatible; planner's call). Constraint: identity must NOT go in the URL — 'me' stays in localStorage ('chat.me'); a shared link must never switch the viewer's identity. Unknown/stale params fail soft to the current default view. Key file: apps/chat/public/app.js (init, selectConversation, openThread, closeThread); no server changes expected.
data.title: Chat: query-string URL state — current channel/DM/thread survives refresh, links shareable

data.description:
Board request via DM (chat msg 59, human:forrest): "I think we need query string to keep page context in here. also, the lattice events should link to the lattice site" — this task is the second half (lattice events link to the lattice site); the query-string half is AS-9.

Interpretation decision (Owen, 2026-08-30): 'the lattice site' = the read-only web dashboard that ships with the Lattice CLI — 'lattice dashboard', default http://127.0.0.1:8799 — which supports per-task deep links via hash routes: #/task/<full-task-id>. No other lattice-viewing surface exists (nothing hosted, nothing in-repo). The chat server already resolves AS-n short codes to full task IDs (lib/lattice.js resolveShortId → taskId), so the link is <base>/#/task/<taskId>.

Scope: AS-n refs in chat messages — at minimum in #lattice-events system messages, sensibly everywhere refs render — gain a working hyperlink to the dashboard task page. Keep the existing in-app task panel (title/status hover context is good); add an 'open in Lattice' link there too. Dashboard base URL configurable (env var, e.g. LATTICE_DASHBOARD_URL, default http://127.0.0.1:8799) since the port is a dashboard default, not a contract. Key files: apps/chat/public/app.js (bodyNode, showTaskPanel), apps/chat/server.js (pass base URL or expose in task payload).

Caveat on record: the link only resolves while 'lattice dashboard' is running locally. Planner may scope in having compose.yaml (or docs) bring the dashboard up alongside chat, or leave that as a follow-up. Rejected alternative: linking to task files on the GitHub remote (https://github.com/malls/american-software) — works without a running dashboard but lands on raw event logs/snapshots, not a task view; revisit only if the board prefers a zero-infrastructure target.
data.title: Chat: AS-n refs and lattice events link out to the Lattice dashboard (#/task/<id>)

data.description: Found during AS-8 review (qa-priya, hostile-fixture attack; does not violate any AS-8 acceptance criterion — defense-in-depth backlog item). Two prototype-chain leaks in apps/chat/lib/lattice.js assignmentsByActor(): (1) the in-flight filter uses `task.status in IN_FLIGHT_RANK`, and `in` walks the prototype chain — a task JSON with status "constructor"/"toString"/etc passes the filter and renders as phantom work (verified in-container: status "constructor" appeared as 'AS-92 · constructor'; textContent rendering means no XSS, wrong data only). (2) the accumulator is a plain object, so `byActor[task.assigned_to] ??= []` with assigned_to "__proto__" reads Object.prototype (non-nullish) and the following .push throws TypeError (verified in-container). Server impact: /api/roster's try/catch swallows it, silently blanking the ENTIRE roster on one hostile task file; CLI 'chat roster' impact: unhandled crash. Trigger requires a hand-crafted .lattice/tasks/*.json (the lattice CLI never writes such values), hence low priority. Fix sketch: filter with Object.hasOwn(IN_FLIGHT_RANK, task.status), accumulate in a Map, return Object.fromEntries(map) (fromEntries uses CreateDataProperty so a '__proto__' key becomes a safe own property). Add regression fixtures: status 'constructor', assigned_to '__proto__'. Repro fixtures used in review are described here; rebuild from this description.
data.title: chat: harden assignmentsByActor against prototype-chain task fields
Watcher hardening nits from AS-7 review (lock steal race, sentinel tmp suffix, SIGKILL timer)

data.description: Discovered in AS-7 first-fire ops verification (2026-08-30): the watcher fired correctly for messageId 120, but the spawned tick died in ~2s with 'Not logged in - Please run /login'. Diagnosis (orchestrator-verified via env -i tests): claude auth on this host is macOS-Keychain-based and requires USER in the process environment; the watcher's child env is exactly {PATH, HOME} per the AS-7 plan's minimal-env rule — one variable too strict. 'env -i HOME=... USER=... PATH=... claude -p' works; without USER it reproduces the failure. THE FIX: apps/chat/watch/advance-watcher.mjs, fire(), child env construction (currently 'env: { PATH: process.env.PATH, HOME: process.env.HOME }', line ~371) — add USER, and consider LOGNAME for the same keychain/identity reason. Do NOT widen further: the minimal-env principle stands, and each added variable needs a stated reason. Also update the comment above the spawn call to record why USER is present. Tests: apps/chat/test/watcher.test.js does not currently assert child env contents (verified by grep), but Priya's AS-7 review verified 'child env exactly {PATH, HOME}' from source — that pin is now stale and must be understood as {PATH, HOME, USER(, LOGNAME)}; if any assertion pinning the env exists or is added, it pins the new set. Priority high: this blocks the chat app as the board's primary interface — every message-triggered tick dies at auth until fixed.
data.title: advance-watcher: pass USER (keychain auth) in tick child env

data.description: Bug #2 from the AS-7 first-fire shakeout (see AS-7 comment 2026-08-30). Deadlock in the lock protocol: apps/chat/watch/advance-watcher.mjs fire() acquires apps/chat/data/advance.lock (source:'watcher', watcher pid) BEFORE spawning claude -p '/advance'. The spawned tick runs advance.md step 0, sees a fresh lock it cannot attribute to itself, and no-ops. advance.md already says 'ticks fired by the message watcher skip this step' — but the spawned tick cannot detect that it IS watcher-fired: the headless invocation is byte-identical to a manual one. Every watcher-fired tick therefore self-cancels. Evidence: apps/chat/data/logs/tick-2026-08-30T18-08-30.241Z.log (tick exited 0, 'Tick ended as a no-op — lock is held', lock pid 17730 == live watcher pid). DESIGN (decided by cto-owen, rationale in plan): watcher passes ADVANCE_TICK_PARENT=watcher:<pid> in the tick child env; advance.md step 0 changes to: a lock whose source is 'watcher' AND whose pid matches ADVANCE_TICK_PARENT is YOUR lock — proceed, and do NOT release it (the watcher releases its own lock in settle() on tick exit); locks from any other source/pid are foreign — no-op. Requires widening the AS-14 env pin {PATH,HOME,USER,LOGNAME} by exactly this one documented variable in tickChildEnv() plus its pin test. Alternatives rejected: (a) watcher releases the lock pre-spawn and lets the tick take its own — opens a real race window between release and the child's step 0 where a manual tick or loop steals the slot, and breaks the watcher's settle()/timeout ownership semantics; (b) advance.md adopts ANY fresh source:watcher lock without a marker — misfires when a manual tick races a watcher fire: the manual tick would adopt the watcher's lock and proceed, defeating single-flight. The env marker is deterministic parent identification: no race, no ambiguity, one documented env var. advance.md is employee-editable; the step-0 wording change is in scope for the implementer.
data.title: Watcher-fired ticks self-cancel on the watcher's own advance.lock — pass ADVANCE_TICK_PARENT marker so the tick recognizes its parent's lock
Harden advance.lock adoption against pid reuse: per-fire nonce in lock file + ADVANCE_TICK_PARENT marker

data.description: Board request (chat DM @human:forrest, msg 116, 2026-08-30 17:43), verbatim: "thread chat is auto scrolling to the bottom on an interval - we should maintain scroll position. also, set me as the default user". Two items: (1) the poll-driven re-render jams the thread panel scroll to the bottom — preserve scroll position across poll re-renders (planner: check whether the main message list has the same defect); (2) when localStorage("chat.me") is unset, the UI should default to human:forrest instead of forcing a manual identity pick. NOTE: the thread sidebar itself is slated for replacement under the threads-inline/modal task (msg 119) — fix the scroll behavior at the poll/render level so it survives that redesign; do not couple the two tasks.
data.title: Chat: thread view must keep scroll position across polls; default identity = human:forrest

data.description: Board request (chat DM @human:forrest, msg 118, 2026-08-30 17:49), verbatim: "also, we should be able to pin employees in the DM list section, then otherwise sort them by team prefix." Interpretation left to the planner, with hints: pinning is a per-viewer preference (localStorage is the established per-viewer store — identity already lives there); "team prefix" most cheaply reads as the actor-id role prefix (developer-, qa-, pm-, ceo-, cto-), though personnel frontmatter also carries a team: field via apps/chat/lib/personnel.js (AS-8) — planner picks one and says why. Touches the AS-8 roster/DM sidebar rendering.
data.title: Chat: pin employees in the DM sidebar; sort unpinned DMs by team prefix

data.description: Board request (chat DM @human:forrest, msg 119, 2026-08-30 17:50), verbatim: "also threads should just appear inline or in a large modal, and not in a sidebar. the sidebar is too narrow to read effectively". Design constraints: (1) AS-9 URL contract — ?t=<message-id> opens the thread rooted at that message and is the ONLY deep-link scheme into chat; the new inline/modal presentation must keep honoring t= links exactly (README "Deep links (AS-9)" section governs). (2) The roster/DM sidebar (AS-8) is a separate surface — replacing the THREAD panel must not disturb it. (3) The thread-scroll bug (AS-17) is being fixed at poll/render level independently; do not wait on it or duplicate it. Inline vs large modal is the planner-level choice — pick one, justify it in the plan.
data.title: Chat: threads render inline or in a large modal — retire the narrow thread sidebar

data.description: Third first-fire attempt (tick log apps/chat/data/logs/tick-2026-08-30T18-20-03.664Z.log): the tick AUTHENTICATED (AS-14 keychain fix works) but ended as a no-op. Root cause: the headless permission layer (claude -p, permission-mode acceptEdits) DENIES environment-variable reads — the tick log states verbatim "the env read was declined by the permission layer" — so the tick could not read ADVANCE_TICK_PARENT and, per the AS-15 rule in advance.md step 0 (a lock it cannot positively claim as its parent is foreign), correctly self-cancelled on its own parent watcher lock. AS-15 chose the right marker but the wrong transport: env vars are not readable inside a headless tick. FIX (transport change, design decided at triage): carry the marker in the PROMPT. The watcher fires claude -p "/advance watcher:<pid>" — the marker rides as the /advance slash-command argument; advance.md declares the argument and step 0 matches the advance.lock pid against the ARGUMENT marker, no env read needed. Keep setting ADVANCE_TICK_PARENT in tickChildEnv as belt-and-suspenders (harmless, and useful in any context where env IS readable), but the prompt argument becomes the contract. Files: apps/chat/watch/advance-watcher.mjs fire() argv; .claude/commands/advance.md (argument declaration + step 0 wording — NOTE advance.md is a .claude command file, not a top-level markdown, so employees may edit it); apps/chat/test/watcher.test.js (pin the spawn argv the way tickChildEnv is pinned). Related: AS-16 (pid-reuse nonce) should ride this same prompt-arg transport when built — its design depends on this contract. NOT in scope / NOT a bug: the "watcher re-fired message 120 three times" observation in that tick log is a misdiagnosis from missing context — those were deliberate board-side highwater resets during debugging; the highwater logic is correct. Do not file or fix anything for it.
data.title: advance-watcher: pass the parent-lock marker in the /advance prompt argument — headless permission layer denies env reads

data.description:
Evidence (tick log apps/chat/data/logs/tick-2026-08-30T19-14-54.450Z.log): project-scope .claude/settings.json permission allowlists are INERT for headless `claude -p` children. The 19:14:54Z tick tested four commands the committed allowlist (65d567e, file mtime 19:13:56Z — on disk before spawn) explicitly allows: `lattice list` [Bash(lattice *)], `node -e` [Bash(node *)], `rtk --version` [Bash(rtk *)], `git add --dry-run` [Bash(git *)] — all four denied. The log's header line gives the mechanism: 'Ignoring 9 permissions.allow entries from .claude/settings.json: this workspace has not been trusted' — a headless child never sees the trust dialog, so project-scope allow rules never load. Read-only commands that still work pass via the built-in read-only heuristic, not our rules. This disproves rung 1 of the permission ladder in apps/chat/watch/README.md:94.

FIX (board + orchestrator selected the tick's proposed fix #2): tickArgv() in apps/chat/watch/advance-watcher.mjs gains --allowedTools carrying exactly the grants from .claude/settings.json's allow list, and --disallowedTools carrying its deny list. The three force-push deny rules MUST survive — that is the git-methodology rule (force-push is always needs_human) riding on this change.

OPEN DESIGN QUESTION for the planner, decide and record why: (a) read .claude/settings.json at fire time — single source of truth, no drift; or (b) hardcode the list in tickArgv with a comment pointing at settings.json — simpler, but two places to update. CTO's read going in: fire-time read is ~6 lines with node's JSON parsing and eliminates drift, which is the exact failure class that caused this bug (settings said allowed, runtime said denied).

Verified flag syntax (claude --help, 2026-08-30): --allowedTools / --disallowedTools are variadic, 'comma or space-separated list' — the watcher spawns without a shell, so each rule rides as its own argv element.

Test impact: apps/chat/test/watcher.test.js:332 pins the exact tickArgv argv array and must account for dynamically-loaded rules; test any settings loader against a fixture settings file, not the live repo file.
data.title: advance-watcher: pass permission grants via --allowedTools/--disallowedTools in tickArgv() — project settings allowlist is inert for headless ticks

data.description:
Board request via chat (msg 148, human:forrest, #board, 2026-08-30 18:59Z), verbatim: "okay, lets make a #bizdev board with us and the new hires"

Gap (scoped across the two prior no-op ticks): store.createChannel() in apps/chat/lib/store.js already supports visibility:'private' + members, but the CLI at apps/chat/bin/chat.js:144-150 hardcodes public and passes neither — #board only exists because store.js:77-84 seeds it. Add `chat create-channel --visibility private --members <id,id,...>` support so restricted channels can be created without seed-code changes.

Acceptance scenario: create #bizdev as a private channel with membership = founders (agent:ceo-carla, agent:cto-owen) + the new research hires (agent:researcher-nadia, agent:researcher-elliot) + human:forrest ('us and the new hires').

Sequencing note: message 148 is still UNDELIVERED to Carla (blocked ticks could not mark reads). The first unblocked tick should deliver it via the normal inbox pull; Carla executes the #bizdev creation once this CLI support lands. This task is the CLI change only — the channel creation itself is Carla's act on the request.
data.title: chat CLI: create-channel gains --visibility private + --members — unblock #bizdev board request

data.description:
Board request, DM msg 163, 2026-08-30 20:41Z, verbatim: "Also, I'm going to be using this on my phone so let's make it layout mobile friendly". Context: the board member's primary interface with the company is this chat app (CLAUDE.md), and he will use it from a phone — mobile is a first-class surface, not a nice-to-have.

Scope — what 'mobile friendly' means for this app: the web UI at apps/chat/public must be usable on a phone-sized viewport (~375-430px wide). Concretely: (1) responsive layout — the sidebar (channels + DM roster) must not consume the viewport; collapse it behind a toggle/drawer on narrow screens, with the message pane full-width; (2) touch targets and font sizes adequate for touch (no tiny click zones); (3) viewport meta + no horizontal scroll; (4) compose box usable with the on-screen keyboard (doesn't get hidden, input stays visible); (5) the AS-9 URL-state contract keeps working so links shared from phone/desktop open the same view.

Relationship to the other chat UX tasks (all bumped per board msg 160 "let's get going on all the chat UX improvements"): AS-17 (thread scroll position + default identity) is independent. AS-18 (DM pinning/sort) touches the same sidebar this task collapses — coordinate, land AS-18 after or fold its sidebar markup in. AS-19 (threads inline or large modal, retiring the narrow thread sidebar) INTERACTS directly: the thread presentation chosen there determines the mobile thread UX (a modal is naturally full-screen on mobile; inline needs its own narrow-viewport treatment). Sequence AS-19 before this task so the mobile layout is built against the final thread presentation, not the retiring sidebar.

Acceptance: chat is fully usable — read, switch conversations, post, open threads, mark read — in a 390px-wide viewport with no horizontal scroll; desktop layout unchanged.
data.title: Chat UI: mobile-friendly responsive layout
